name: Articles: il, lo, la, l', i, gli, le; un, uno, una, un'

regional.note: In the north and in Tuscany people often put la before a woman's first name (la Giulia). The standard and the south say just Giulia.

subtitle: Italian has seven words for “the”: il, lo, l', la, i, gli, le, and four for “a”: un, uno, una, un'. The article matches the noun (masculine or feminine, one or more), and it also depends on the first sound of the noun: il libro, lo studente, l'amico.

flow.text: il / lo / l' / la · i / gli / le

concept.exampleHtml: un libro → il libro · uno zaino → lo zaino · un amico → l'amico · una chiave → la chiave · i libri · gli zaini · le chiavi

qa.html: Masculine, one: il before most consonants: il libro, il medico. lo before s + consonant, z, gn, ps and y: lo studente, lo zaino, lo psicologo, lo yogurt. l' before a vowel: l'amico, l'ufficio.
Masculine, more than one: i for the il words: i libri, i medici. gli for the lo and l' words: gli studenti, gli zaini, gli amici, gli uffici.
Feminine: la, and l' before a vowel: la casa, la chiave, l'amica, l'ora. The plural is always le: le case, le amiche, le ore.
“A”: un for the il and l' words: un libro, un amico (no apostrophe). uno for the lo words: uno studente, uno zaino. una for feminine words: una casa, and un' before a vowel: un'amica, un'ora.
il, lo, la mean “the”: something you both know. La farmacia è qui. un, uno, una mean “a”: something new. C'è una farmacia qui vicino?
Usually no article with a job after essere: Sono infermiera. (You also hear Faccio l'infermiera.) No article with a language after parlare: Parlo arabo.

concept.noteHtml: Common mistakes: ✗ il studente → ✓ lo studente. ✗ i amici → ✓ gli amici. ✗ un'amico → ✓ un amico (the apostrophe is only for feminine words). Not sure about the gender? See Nouns and gender. Prepositions with the article (al, del, nel) come at A2: Prepositions with articles.

s + consonant, z, gn, ps, y (masc.)

items: Masculine before a vowel: un, no apostrophe. Un amico, un ufficio.
Feminine before a vowel: un'. Un'amica, un'ora.
Names of people and cities: Giulia, Milano.

listen.note: una: a new thing, one of many.
la: we both know which one.
gli: the plural of l' and lo.

hoeren.instruction: Listen and choose the sentence you heard. You can listen twice.

rounds.label: 1 · From un to il
rounds.instruction: You hear a noun with un, uno, una or un'. Say it with il, lo, la or l'.

rounds.label: 2 · One to many
rounds.instruction: You hear a noun with the article. Say it in the plural.

exercises.title: il, lo or l'? Masculine nouns.
exercises.hint: Most consonants: il. s + consonant, z, ps: lo. A vowel: l'.

exercises.title: i, gli or le? The plural.
exercises.hint: Masculine: i, or gli before a vowel, s + consonant and z. Feminine: always le.

exercises.title: un, uno, una or un'?
exercises.hint: The same sound rule: uno before s + consonant and z, un' only for feminine words before a vowel.

exercises.title: The or a?
exercises.hint: Something new: un, una. Something you both know, or there is only one: il, la, l'.

items.prompt: Ho una macchina nuova. ___ macchina è rossa.

exercises.title: Which form? The first sound decides.
exercises.hint: lo, uno, gli before s + consonant and z. l' and gli before a vowel. un' only for feminine words.

exercises.hint: First find the gender and the number. Then look at the first sound of the noun.
